rationale: B wins because it makes the 22% pilot claim the spine of an actual reported story: "Without the baseline, 22% is unpublishable." That is the adult in the room. A has good instincts, but "Mindbody's AI treats 50,000 studios' booking calendars as one data set" turns scale into an unproven data-pooling claim. Both sets need fact work before pitching; B does a better job telling the founder exactly where the story will break.
gaps_in_A: "Mindbody's AI treats 50,000 studios' booking calendars as one data set" is not in the update. The facts say Mindbody powers booking for 50,000 studios and uses booking data; they do not say it pools all calendars into one data set.

"Mindbody owns the software studios run on and the marketplace that fills their classes — and it's adding AI to both" overstates the product. The update gives a studio-side scheduling assistant, not AI being added to ClassPass.

"The AI upgrade boutique fitness startups promised just shipped from the incumbent instead" invents a competitive field and a promise from startups. The proof section admits it needs a named competitor; until then, it is theater.
"private-equity ownership and monetization strategy" assumes the nature of the post-take-private ownership before proving it. Fine as a question, too firm as the premise of an angle.
gaps_in_B: "studios get it whether or not they asked for it" turns bundled pricing into forced adoption. Bundled into tiers does not mean automatically enabled across the customer base.

"That's a live change to how 50,000+ businesses run their schedules" overclaims reach. Mindbody powers booking for 50,000 studios and salons; the update does not say all of them will use this assistant.

"The company that owns ClassPass now decides which classes fill first" is too prosecutorial for the facts. The update does not say Mindbody prioritizes members, routes demand, or lets ClassPass influence waitlist filling.
"front desks stopped having time to do" smuggles in a staffing-workload story the update never supplied. It may be true, but a reporter will ask for evidence and you do not have it yet.
